review_limits: No paper draft was supplied (review target was restricted to the slide diff in slides_ssha2026.tex and the brief); paper-wide claims-vs-code verification could not be performed beyond the slide and code comments.
The external census and FamilySearch profile datasets on external drives (F: and Dropbox) were not directly readable, and the full Stata pipeline was not runnable in this review environment.
Runtime verification of exact numbers relies on the verified execution log (MATCHING/profile_names_jw.log) and embedded do-file assertion checks rather than fresh pipeline re-execution.
structured_output.summary: The slide update and supporting do-file changes are verified correct and consistent. Every statistic in the slide table matches the corresponding section and column of MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md, the sample restrictions and column definitions are accurately described, and the post-run edits to the do-file do not alter any numerical results. The slide explicitly clarifies that FamilySearch profiles reflect agreement rather than ground-truth accuracy.

verified_clean.evidence: Checked all 20 numerical values in slides_ssha2026.tex:362-366 against MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md lines 11, 13, 23, and 25. Men Target (disc) records (6,344,776), exact agreement (Ancestry 17.0%, Ours 51.9%), and full name JW (Ancestry 0.906, Ours 0.939) match lines 9-13; Men All records (26,230,508), exact agreement (Ancestry 59.1%, Ours 65.0%), and full name JW (Ancestry 0.946, Ours 0.951) match line 11; Women Target (disc) records (6,020,539), exact first agreement (Ancestry 53.7%, Ours 68.2%), and first name JW (Ancestry 0.896, Ours 0.919) match lines 21-25; Women All records (22,952,453), exact first agreement (Ancestry 72.2%, Ours 75.4%), and first name JW (Ancestry 0.925, Ours 0.930) match line 23.
verified_clean.item: Slide table values match profile_names_jw.md exactly across all rows and columns

verified_clean.evidence: slides_ssha2026.tex:336-353,371-373 accurately document the sample restrictions (1940 census, 49 model states, 4 human name fields present, 1:1 linked to FS profile without sex contradiction and with death month), gender-specific scoring (both names and average JW for men, first name only for women), and the 'model names present' restriction without fallback to Ancestry (matching MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:85-155). The slide comments also correctly explain why Ancestry's target agreement is higher for women (women's target includes records where surnames disagree but first names agree, while scoring is on first names only).
verified_clean.item: Slide text and comments match sample definitions and scoring rules in the code

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:135-155 defines hasml as `(men & hm_f & hm_l) | (wom & hm_f)` where hm_f and hm_l verify non-empty normalized model first name and surname after pnorm normalisation (cf_ml!="" and cl_ml!=""). Both Ancestry and Ours are summarized under this identical restriction in MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:222.
verified_clean.item: Model-present indicator (hasml) strictly implements the stated condition

verified_clean.evidence: The two edits in MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do (adding an explanatory sentence in the file write header at line 197 and replacing empty cell display with '-' when r(N)==0 at line 225) only alter output formatting and documentation; they modify no data variables or estimation routines.
verified_clean.item: Post-run do-file edits do not affect numerical calculations

verified_clean.item: Hand-edited markdown matches do-file output formatting

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
